As of 320 PM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Patchy fog possible overnight, followed by a  
warming trend that will bring above normal temperatures late in
the week, along with dry conditions.

The latest WX analysis indicates an upper level trough still in
place along the east coast, with an upper ridge developing from
the western Gulf coast to the lower OH Valley. At the surface,
low pressure lingers off the coast of Maine and is slowly moving
farther offshore to Atlantic Canada, while weak high pressure is
situated across the local area. The light onshore flow for most
of our region combined with somewhat of a cold pool aloft in 
association with the upper trough has kept the clouds around today
with just a few breaks noted on the latest satellite imagery.
Temperatures are seasonable, mostly in the mid to upper 70s. For
tonight, the winds will be light and variable inland and light
onshore near the coast. Have increased the cloud cover into the
early evening given the latest trends. The setup will be favorable
for fog overnight/early Wednesday morning if the sky does see 
clearing this evening. However, if the clouds stay more prevalent,
then fog development would be less likely so confidence is 
rather low in the extent of this later tonight, but will
continue with the mention of patchy fog for most of the area
after midnight. Lows will range from the upper 50s in the
piedmont to the mid-upper 60s/around 70F near the coast in the 
SE. On Wednesday, we should finally see at least a partly sunny
sky as the low level flow shifts to the S-SE by afternoon with
the high sliding offshore. There is still enough low level
moisture to keep some SCT-BKN clouds around and if fog does
materialize overnight, it could be mostly cloudy for much of the
morning timeframe. Highs will rise to around 80F across the
north and low-mid 80s elsewhere. There is a higher confidence 
for a mostly sunny sky with temperatures becoming very warm 
Thursday and Friday as the low level S-SW flow increases. Still
not anticipating record highs, but highs into the upper 80s
Thursday, with upper 80s to lower 90s Friday is about 10-15 F
above average for the start of October and qualifies as
"unseasonably warm". 

KEY MESSAGE 2...An unsettled weather pattern with cooler and 
wetter conditions appears likely for this weekend into early 
next week.

An increasingly unsettled pattern looks to take shape for the
weekend into early next week. A deep closed low currently over 
the Desert Southwest into the Intermountain West looks to open 
up by midweek as it absorbs the mid-level remnants of TC Polo 
and lifts across the central and southern Plains. This system 
will eventually become absorbed into a northern stream trough 
digging across the interior Northeast into the northern Mid- 
Atlantic over the weekend. This will serve to dampen the Southeast
ridge and allow an influx of Gulf and Pacific moisture across 
the Gulf Coast and Mid-South, likely reaching our region over 
the weekend. There is still considerable spread among the 
probabilistic model guidance regarding the exact timing and 
track of these features, but a cold front is likely to push
south through much of the area on Saturday, then stall, with
additional (and more significant moisture) riding along the 
front later in the weekend into early next week. While some low-
end rain chances accompany the initial windshift Saturday, the 
higher chances are expected late Saturday night/early Sunday 
through at least early Monday. One signal common to all 
guidance, even this far out, is a notable increase in PWATs, 
with values potentially reaching 1.5-2" by Saturday 
night/Sunday. There is still plenty of time to monitor the 
trends over the next several days, but locally heavy rainfall is
certainly possible (although much of this would be beneficial 
given ongoing drought). In terms of temperatures, increased 
clouds/precip and onshore flow favor cooler temps over the 
weekend into early next week, but not abnormally so. Highs 
Saturday likely range through the 70s and 80s, with higher PoPs 
and cloud cover bringing cooler upper 60s and 70s Sunday and 
Monday. Latest models indicate a strong enough push of drier 
air associated with high pressure building in from the north 
into the middle of next week, which would bring below normal 
temperatures with highs in the 60s and lows into the 40s and 
50s- this is still more uncertain given the range.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Low-end tidal flooding this evening across the
Bayside of the lower Maryland eastern shore. 

Low-end tidal flooding continues to impact vulnerable sites mostly 
due to the lunar cycle and resulting higher astronomical tide. It is 
generally action stage nuisance flooding, but a few sites such as 
Bishops Head and Crisfield will enter minor stage with the upcoming 
high tide this evening. A Coastal Flood Statement was issued for the 
bay side of the MD Eastern Shore through 9pm tonight.
